elements.element: Audit frequency limited to no more than once per 12 months
elements.evidence: "not more than once in any twelve (12) month period"

elements.element: At least 30 days' prior written notice
elements.evidence: "upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company"

elements.element: Audit conducted by an independent auditor
elements.evidence: "HDI's General Manager ... have the right to inspect the records" — the auditing person is Vendor's own officer, not an independent auditor
No confidentiality undertaking attaches to the inspecting party anywhere in the redlined clause
"The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI."

elements.element: Cost shifts to Customer only where underpayment exceeds 5%
elements.evidence: No cost-shift carve-back exists; Vendor bears cost unconditionally, which is at least as protective for us

elements.element: No direct access to Customer systems
elements.evidence: Clause grants a right to "inspect the records of the Company's General Manager" with no express prohibition on direct access to Customer systems

elements.element: Audit no more than once per year
elements.evidence: "not more than once in any twelve (12) month period"
"no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice" exceeds the 15-day floor

elements.element: Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%
elements.evidence: "fees incurred by HDI ... shall be borne by HDI" with no shift-back trigger

reasons: Locked target was preferred, but the edit only added the frequency cap; the preferred position's independent-auditor requirement, the auditor confidentiality binding, and the express bar on direct access to Customer systems remain absent (the inspector is still "HDI's General Manager").

Fallback is fully satisfied on its material terms: once per twelve months, 30 days' notice (better than 15), and Vendor-borne cost with no shift-back threshold, so the clause sits at the fallback and is acceptable rather than a deviation.
Absence of a 5%/10% cost-shift trigger operates in our favour (Vendor bears cost unconditionally) and is not a gap to close.

Minimality: the operation inserts only the short phrase "not more than once in any twelve (12) month period and" plus a comma into the existing sentence; the official gate's failure is a mechanical word-ratio artefact of quoting the surrounding anchor text, not surplus operative language. A pure insertion anchored on "may" would clear the ratio if the gate must be satisfied.
No undefined terms, contradictions or dangling mechanics introduced; notice, business-hours and cost sentences are untouched.
Margin comment accurately describes the change and the unchanged terms.
